Diagnose sensitivity to HMM-SSF starting values

Source: R/restarts.R
diagnose_ssf_restarts.Rd

Fit the same model from different starting values. Each run uses the same steps and control sets, if supplied. The restart log shows which fits pass the taxonomy checks and whether the optimiser agrees with the forward likelihood calculation.

Usage

diagnose_ssf_restarts(
  data,
  taxonomy,
  n_starts = 30L,
  seed = NULL,
  spread = 0.5,
  short_iter = 100L,
  long_iter = 900L,
  engine = c("native", "R"),
  normalization = if (inherits(data, "ssf_steps")) "exact" else "importance",
  starts = NULL,
  formula = NULL,
  target = "cos_diff_theta_to_target",
  assessment_args = list(),
  likelihood_tol = 1e-05,
  parameter_tol = 0.001,
  objective_tol = 1e-07,
  step_family = NULL,
  keep_rejected = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Observed ssf_steps or case-control data for fit_ssf(). Case-control data must have a density measure declared.

taxonomy

A specification from ssf_taxonomy() or a built-in name accepted by assess_taxonomy().

n_starts

Number of random starts, used when starts is NULL.

seed

Optional seed for the whole search. The previous RNG state is restored on exit.

spread, short_iter, long_iter, engine

Fitting controls for fit_ssf().

normalization

Defaults to "exact" for ssf_steps and "importance" for case-control data.

starts

Optional list of start specifications that replaces the default random starts. Each entry is a list with optional seed, spread and initial_values arguments for fit_ssf(). An empty list entry uses the default random initialisation. Names of entries are optional group labels and may repeat.

formula

Optional formula override. Defaults to the custom taxonomy formula or the built-in movement formula with a target term for HDT.

target

Name of the target coefficient for the built-in HDT taxonomy.

assessment_args

Optional named list of thresholds for assess_taxonomy(), for example list(min_occupancy = 0.10).

likelihood_tol, parameter_tol

Absolute grouping tolerances for log likelihood and aligned working parameters.

objective_tol

Maximum allowed difference between the optimiser and forward log likelihood.

step_family

Optional length family passed to fit_ssf().

keep_rejected

Retain each successful optimisation in all_fits, including taxonomically rejected fits, for reassessment without refitting. Errors remain NULL. Default FALSE limits memory use.

Value

An ssf_restarts object with solutions ranked by likelihood, states with movement and occupancy summaries for each solution, restarts with one outcome per start, attempts with optimiser logs, and fits with the representative ssf_fit objects. Solution numbers are scoped to this search. Use compare_ssf_solutions() for step labels.

Details

The search groups fits that give the same Viterbi labels and have similar likelihoods and parameters once their states are aligned by label. It works from highest to lowest likelihood and compares each fit to the existing representatives in that order. The parameter tolerance applies to the largest absolute difference on the fitting scale, including log transition odds relative to self-transition. Restart counts depend on the starting values tried.

See also

compare_ssf_solutions(), plot_ssf_changes()

Examples

gps <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "deer-restart-steps.rds",
  package = "behavSSF"))
steps <- prepare_ssf_steps(gps, density_measure = "area")
labels <- ssf_taxonomy("step_lengths", c("Short steps", "Long steps"))
check <- diagnose_ssf_restarts(steps, labels, n_starts = 6, seed = 60200)
check$solutions
#>   solution representative_start log_likelihood delta_log_likelihood n_restarts
#> 1        1                    1       59.65201             0.000000          2
#> 2        2                    4       52.38869             7.263316          4
#>   n_changed_vs_best
#> 1                 0
#> 2               325
